item.title: Transformer Seismic Design: What Should Substation Engineers Consider?
item.description:
High-voltage transformers are critical assets in transmission substations, and their mechanical performance can become particularly important during seismic events. Transformer seismic design is not limited to the transformer tank itself. Engineers may need to consider the complete installed arrangement, including: • Transformer anchoring and foundations
• Bushings and their mechanical withstand capability
• Conservator and supporting structures
• Flexible connections and interfaces
• Cable and conductor movement
• Auxiliary equipment and control cabinets
• Overall equipment and substation resilience

Electro Lounge Discussion:
When specifying transformers and substation equipment, how should seismic qualification be addressed in regions traditionally considered to have relatively low seismic risk?

Share your engineering experience and perspective with the Electro Lounge community.

item.title: Industry Navigator 2026 Kicks Off in Vienna, Spotlighting Key T&D Sector Trends
item.description: Industry Navigator 2026 has officially opened in Vienna, bringing together professionals from across the transmission and distribution (T&D) sector for a focused three-day event. The conference opens with in-depth sessions dedicated to the current and future state of supply chains, sector growth, and the evolving challenges that will influence the next phase of T&D development. For electrical industry professionals, the discussions promise valuable insights into strategies and technological advancements that are shaping the future of power delivery infrastructure. By addressing both business and technical aspects—highlighted by leading publications in the field—participants can expect practical perspectives on navigating supply chain disruptions and harnessing opportunities for industry progress.

item.title: Netel Secures $3.2M Contract for E.ON Substation Project in Sweden
item.description: Netel has been awarded a $3.2 million contract for a new substation project in partnership with E.ON, set in Bollstabruk, Sweden. The project is scheduled for completion in 2029 and marks a notable investment in the region's electrical infrastructure. Substations are critical elements in grid development, supporting the safe and reliable transmission and distribution of electricity. For professionals involved in power infrastructure and grid modernization, developments like this play a key role in strengthening system resilience and capacity. This project not only reflects ongoing efforts to enhance energy delivery in Sweden, but also offers opportunities for engineering, construction, and ongoing technical collaboration within the sector.

item.title: National Grid Initiative Aims to Accelerate Industrial Grid Connections in New South Wales
item.description: A new programme in New South Wales is exploring the use of battery storage and other methods to increase existing grid capacity for industrial customers. This initiative focuses on testing flexible grid connection solutions, with the goal of enabling faster access for industrial sites requiring significant electrification. By evaluating new approaches to grid management, the project could set a foundation for more responsive and adaptive energy infrastructure. These efforts reflect a broader push to support industrial growth while effectively managing available electrical resources. For professionals in the power sector, this development highlights the growing importance of integrating storage and flexible connection strategies to address current grid constraints.

item.title: Offshore Substations Set Sail for Major Baltic Sea Wind Project
item.description: Two offshore substations, each with a capacity of approximately 450 MW, are now en route to the German sector of the Baltic Sea to support the grid connection for the 927 MW Gennaker wind farm. This development represents an important milestone in advancing the integration of offshore wind energy into the mainland transmission network. The substations are integral to efficiently collecting and transmitting power generated offshore, underlining the vital role of high-capacity, reliable infrastructure in supporting large-scale renewable energy projects. For professionals involved in design, operation, or maintenance of electrical networks, this deployment provides a significant example of scaling up offshore grid connectivity while aligning with growing renewable generation targets.

item.title: National Grid Invests $6.5 Million in Live-Line Maintenance Innovation
item.description: National Grid has secured $6.5 million in funding for a three-year initiative focused on advancing live-line maintenance for high-voltage transmission assets. This project aims to develop equipment and refine procedures that allow critical grid infrastructure to be maintained while remaining energized. The initiative is expected to address key challenges in handling insulators, conductors, and other high-voltage components during live operation—an area of growing importance as the grid’s resilience and operational efficiency become even more critical. Electrical professionals and grid operators stand to benefit from the enhanced safety measures and reduced risk of outages associated with improved live-line maintenance techniques.

item.title: Upcoming Webinar to Examine Variable Shunt Reactors and Their Impact on Grid Voltage Stability
item.description: Electrical professionals interested in maintaining reliable grid operations are invited to join a Reinhausen-hosted webinar focused on Variable Shunt Reactors (VSRs). Taking place on Tuesday, October 27, at 2 pm CET, the session will explore the basics of VSRs and their significance in today’s power grids. Attendees can expect to gain insights into reactive power compensation and voltage control strategies—key topics as modern utilities increasingly manage fluctuating load conditions. As understanding and adaptability become critical in evolving grid environments, this educational opportunity will be particularly relevant for those seeking to enhance grid voltage stability. The webinar is highlighted in Transformer Magazine’s news section.

item.title: Texas Unveils $22 Billion Power Campus Integrating Generation and Data Center Demand
item.description: A landmark development is underway in Encinal, Texas, where a new $22 billion power campus is set to reshape regional power supply strategies. Plans call for a 6.47 GW gas-fired power plant designed to directly support a neighboring 5 GW data center, with any surplus generation distributed to the wider Texas grid. This project highlights evolving approaches to meet escalating data center energy needs while reinforcing local grid capacity. For professionals in power generation, grid planning, and energy infrastructure, the integration of large-scale power assets with high-demand facilities signals new opportunities and challenges for managing load, reliability, and resource allocation.

item.title: Major Federal Backing Advances Alaska Transmission Expansion
item.description: A significant milestone for Alaska’s electrical infrastructure has been reached with the U.S. Department of Energy committing support for a new transmission project valued at $418 million. The planned 359-kilometer (223-mile) Beluga-Healy line will establish a second high-voltage link connecting Southcentral and Interior Alaska. This new transmission pathway is poised to enhance grid reliability and resilience for the region, while also supporting the operational capabilities of substations managed by the Alaska Energy Authority. With increased interconnection between previously less-connected regions, this initiative represents a strategic investment in the state’s long-term grid stability and modernization.
